questions.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a private vehicle on an urban road when no sign sets a different limit?
questions.explain: On an urban road, with no sign, the maximum speed is {{fact:speed.urban}} (reg. 54).

questions.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a private vehicle on a non-urban road with no built divider, when there is no sign?
questions.explain: On a non-urban road with no built divider — {{fact:speed.nonurban}}. With a built divider — {{fact:speed.nonurban_divided}}.

questions.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a private vehicle on an expressway when no sign sets a different limit?
questions.explain: On an expressway, with no sign, the maximum speed is {{fact:speed.freeway}}. A sign can set up to {{fact:speed.sign_cap.freeway}}.

questions.q: What counts as a "built divider" for the maximum speed on a non-urban road?
options: A double continuous line painted on the road
A barrier, fence or raised traffic island that physically separates the directions of travel
An extra lane for a slow vehicle on an uphill stretch
Wide shoulders on both sides of the road
questions.explain: A built divider is a physical separation — a barrier, fence or raised island. Painted lines are not a built divider.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed in a traffic-calmed zone?
options: At the driver's discretion, with no numeric limit
questions.explain: On a shared street and in a traffic-calmed zone, the maximum speed is {{fact:speed.traffic_calming}}.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed of a commercial vehicle whose gross vehicle weight is over {{fact:speed.heavy_threshold}} on an expressway?
questions.explain: A heavy commercial vehicle (over {{fact:speed.heavy_threshold}}) is restricted outside the city — even on an expressway — to {{fact:speed.heavy.nonurban}}.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed of a bus (not a minibus) on an expressway with no sign?
questions.explain: A bus is restricted on an expressway to {{fact:speed.bus.freeway}}, and its speed limiter is also set to {{fact:speed.limiter.bus}}.

questions.q: The permitted speed on a stretch of road is {{fact:speed.urban}}. Heavy rain is falling and visibility is poor. What is correct?
options: You must drive at a reasonable speed that suits the conditions — lower than {{fact:speed.urban}} if circumstances require it
You may drive at {{fact:speed.urban}}, because that is the permitted speed
You must stop on the shoulder until the rain stops
You may drive a little above {{fact:speed.urban}} to get out of the rain area quickly
questions.explain: The permitted speed is only an upper limit. The law requires driving at a reasonable speed for all the circumstances and keeping full control of the vehicle (reg. 51).

questions.q: In which of the following situations must a driver slow down?
options: When the road is straight and clear and visibility is good
When approaching the crest of a hill that hides the road ahead
When a vehicle behind wants to overtake
When entering an expressway from an acceleration lane
questions.explain: Before the crest of a hill your field of view is limited, so you must slow down (reg. 52). On an acceleration lane, you instead match your speed to the flow of traffic.

questions.q: When is sudden emergency braking allowed?
options: Any time the driver wants to test the brakes, anywhere
Sudden emergency braking is never allowed
To warn a vehicle that is tailgating
Only to avoid an accident that cannot be avoided any other way, or for safety reasons
questions.explain: Emergency braking is allowed only to avoid an accident or for traffic safety reasons (reg. 53). "Teaching a lesson" to a tailgating driver by braking hard is dangerous and forbidden.

questions.q: What is a vehicle's stopping distance made up of?
questions.explain: Stopping distance = reaction distance (until the foot is on the brake) + braking distance (until the vehicle stops).

questions.q: What is "reaction distance"?
options: The distance the vehicle travels from the moment the driver notices the danger until braking begins
The distance at which the driver can see the road ahead
The distance between the vehicle and the vehicle ahead of it
The distance the vehicle travels from the start of braking until it stops
questions.explain: During the reaction time the vehicle keeps travelling at full speed. The distance it covers in that time is the reaction distance.

questions.q: A driver doubled their speed from 50 to 100 km/h. By roughly how much does the braking distance grow?
questions.explain: Braking distance grows with the square of the speed: double the speed — quadruple the braking distance.

questions.q: Which of the following lengthens a driver's reaction time?
options: Fatigue and talking on the phone
questions.explain: Fatigue, distraction, alcohol and medication lengthen reaction time. Tyres, the road surface and weight affect braking distance.

questions.q: What does the ABS system do under hard braking?
options: It brakes the vehicle on its own when approaching an obstacle
It always shortens the braking distance by half
It sends braking only to the rear wheels
It stops the wheels from locking, so the driver can keep steering while braking
questions.explain: ABS prevents the wheels from locking and preserves steering ability. It does not necessarily shorten the braking distance. In an emergency stop, press hard and do not ease off.

questions.q: What is the minimum time gap the law requires you to keep behind a vehicle driving ahead of you in the same lane?
options: The law sets no minimum time gap
questions.explain: Regulation 49 sets a gap of at least {{fact:following.min_time_gap}} — the legal minimum. The recommendation is to keep at least {{fact:following.recommended_gap}}, and more in difficult conditions.

questions.q: Why is it recommended to measure the gap from the vehicle ahead in seconds rather than metres?
options: Because a gap in seconds grows by itself as speed rises, matching reaction time
Because it is easier to remember a number of seconds
Because the law forbids measuring distance in metres
questions.explain: At higher speed you cover more metres every second. A gap in seconds guarantees a constant reaction time at any speed.

questions.q: In which situation should you increase the gap from the vehicle ahead?
options: When the road is empty of traffic
When the vehicle ahead is large and lets you see well
When driving on a dry road in bright daylight
questions.explain: In the first rain, water mixes with oil and dust that have built up on the road, making it especially slippery. Braking distance lengthens, so you should increase the gap.

questions.q: A vehicle is tailgating you while you drive. What is the safe response?
options: Brake hard so it backs off
Slightly increase the gap from the vehicle ahead of you, so you can brake gradually
Drive on the lane divider line so it cannot overtake
Speed up to get away from it
questions.explain: A large gap ahead lets you brake gently, so the driver behind also has time to react. "Punishing" a tailgater with sudden braking is dangerous and forbidden.

questions.q: Hitting a fixed obstacle at 50 km/h is roughly equivalent to falling from a height of —
questions.explain: At 50 km/h (about 14 metres per second), the kinetic energy equals that of a fall from about 10 metres. At 100 km/h — about 40 metres.

questions.q: By roughly how much does a vehicle's kinetic energy grow when its speed rises from 40 to 80 km/h?
questions.explain: Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed: double the speed — quadruple the energy.

questions.q: A heavy goods vehicle is climbing slowly up a steep hill, and a line of vehicles is building up behind it. The shoulder is paved and clear. What should it do?
options: Accelerate beyond its ability so as not to hold anyone up
Signal left to show that overtaking is forbidden
Keep to the right and drive on the shoulder to let the vehicles behind overtake it
Stay in its lane — it is driving at the permitted speed
questions.explain: A vehicle forced to drive slowly because of a load or a gradient must keep to the right, and where the shoulder is paved and clear — drive on it and allow overtaking (reg. 48).
